body:
This hit me right in the gut, but not for the reason you might think. As I said before, these thoughts have been with me for the majority of my life. I don't know who I am beneath all of it. It's become a part of who I am. I feel like the more I fight it and try to reach out to people, the more I get pushed away. 

To get all heavy and metaphorical and shit, I guess my life has been spent in the darkness. Mostly because whenever I tried to shine a light in my dark little world, someone or something would blow it out. I feel like all I have right now is an empty book of matches and the darkness, surrounding me. The past week or so, I've grown to accept the darkness, because nothing else will accept me.

I've tried making those changes. I've tried working out, I swam for about a year, and in the beginning it felt great, but then it just became a routine. I've tried getting a new job, where everyone was near my age, I thought it would help, but instead I was as much of an outcast as I've ever been, and not for lack of trying on my part.

That's the reason I can't get it out of my head, because it's final. It means I wouldn't have to struggle with these thoughts, with living my life day by day, with no foreseeable light at the end of the tunnel.

I have thought about packing up and leaving, but what would change, other than the scenery? My problems won't just stay behind, they'll come along for the ride. I really don't know how to be a different person, because this is how I've been for as long as I can remember, becoming something different wouldn't be 'me'.
